name: 1605 S. Prairie Avenue — the Illinois Central's 16th Street station (district draft; refined by T-1866)

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads '2-storey frame (yellow) building lettered ILLINOIS CENTRAL R.R. 16TH ST. STATION'. Robinson 1886 shows a frame building lettered 16TH ST. STATION, I.C.R.R. here, so the station use is carried to 1904. Carried to 1904 on the T-1840 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2335, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1866 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 20 trace (s20fp-1605-b1), the T-1840 census (s20-1605-f) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20-023; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1840 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

position.symbolic_location: 1605 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1605 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 2.000, v -6.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check, so its own fit residual, 2.46 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed. Rotation 179.609 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading '2-storey frame (yellow) building lettered ILLINOIS CENTRAL R.R. 16TH ST. STATION': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: frame.

parts.from: s20fp-1605-b1 p1 (main, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 98% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s20fp-1605-b1 p1 (main, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 98% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: Not a house: the sheet letters the two-storey frame building 'ILLINOIS CENTRAL R.R. 16TH ST. STATION' and Robinson 1886 shows a station on the same ground, so the census carries the use to 1904. It stands as the draft's plain two-storey gabled outbuilding with its own name and use; its platforms, canopies and signs are T-1866's. (The register's '1603' row is this frontage; the sheet prints 1605.) Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1355794894 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-16-18-east-2335.
